transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me today. Um, I hope I'm in the right place for this... but I guess I've just been having a little bit of trouble keeping things, you know, perfectly organized lately? 

It's really not a huge deal, I'm probably just overthinking it, but I'm trying to balance my schoolwork and this tiny little accessories shop I run. I just... I kind of let things get a bit jumbled. Like, my craft supplies, my business receipts, and then my assignment notes and due dates... they sort of just end up in these big piles everywhere. And then I just sit there not knowing what I should tackle first. 

Is that... does that make sense? I know everyone gets a little messy sometimes, so I really hope I'm not wasting your time by being here.
Do you find yourself thinking about organizing or fixing these piles of things even when you're not actively working on them?

Um, well, not really? I mean, I definitely want to be organized, and I know I should be... but when I'm away from my desk or out with friends, I'm usually just focused on whatever's happening right then. 

I guess I don't really dwell on the mess when I'm not looking right at it. I hope that doesn't make me sound irresponsible! I really do care about getting it all sorted out eventually. Is it... is it bad that I don't think about it all the time?
Do you often feel anxious or worried about things in general, not just when you're looking at the mess?

Oh, um, no, not really! I actually think I'm a pretty positive person, generally speaking. I don't really sit around worrying about things... I kind of just bounce from one thing to the next, to be honest. 

Maybe I should worry a little more about my responsibilities, haha, but no, I wouldn't say I feel anxious overall. It's really just the physical piles of stuff that overwhelm me when I'm staring right at them. I just... I really hope I'm answering these right. Is that the kind of thing you were asking?
Do you find yourself repeating certain actions or rituals over and over?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I don't have any routines like that. I actually kind of struggle to keep any sort of routine going, if I'm being completely honest. 

I just sort of do things as they come up, you know? I don't have to check things multiple times or do things in a certain order or anything like that. I hope that's a good thing? I know having a routine is supposed to be good for you, but I just... I haven't really managed to stick to one. Is it okay that I don't really have any rituals like that?
Have you noticed any problems in your relationships with friends or family because of your difficulties with organization or time management?

Um, well, my family and close friends are really supportive, so we're mostly okay there! They know I mean well. But, um... I guess it has caused a few issues in other areas. 

I'm actually a little embarrassed to admit this, but... I kind of messed up and missed some required steps for my program recently. And because of that, my financial aid is sort of at risk right now. I feel really awful about it, I really do. 

And, um, the people I work with on our shop projects... I've noticed they've started depending on me a bit less lately. Which I completely understand! I don't blame them at all for stepping back. I just... I hope you don't think I'm completely unreliable or a bad person for letting things get this far. I'm really trying my best to fix it and get back on track. Does that answer what you were asking?
Are you having trouble meeting your basic needs, such as getting enough sleep, eating regularly, or taking care of your personal hygiene due to your organizational challenges?

Oh, no, definitely not! I'm doing just fine with all of that. I mean, I might stay up a little late sometimes working on a project, or grab a quick snack instead of a full meal if I'm in a rush, but nothing major. 

I always make sure I'm showered and presentable, especially when I'm around other people. I wouldn't want anyone to think I'm not taking care of myself! So, yeah, my basic needs are totally met. I'm actually pretty good at making sure I get enough sleep most nights. I hope that's what you were looking for? I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you feel like your difficulties with organization are causing you a lot of stress or emotional upset?

Um, no, I wouldn't say it's causing me a *lot* of stress. I mean, sure, it's a little frustrating sometimes when I misplace things or, you know, with the financial aid thing I mentioned... but I try not to let it get to me too much! 

I really try to stay positive and just keep moving forward. I don't want to sound like I'm complaining or making a big deal out of nothing, because I know other people have it way worse. I'm generally a pretty happy person, honestly! I just need to figure out a better system, that's all. I'm not, like, falling apart over it or anything. Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm not coming across as too scattered.
Are there any activities or tasks that you've had to give up or significantly reduce because of your organizational difficulties?

Um, no, not really. I haven't really had to give anything up. I mean, I still do all the things I enjoy, like working on my shop projects and hanging out with friends. 

I guess sometimes I might, you know, run out of time to do *everything* I wanted to do in a day, but I think that happens to everyone, right? I'm still managing to keep up with my hobbies and everything else. I definitely wouldn't say I've had to significantly reduce anything. I try really hard to balance it all, even if it gets a little messy sometimes. Does that sound okay? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right.
Have you noticed your grades or shop sales suffering because of your organizational challenges?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, my grades are mostly fine, but... well, I did kind of miss a few required steps for my program recently. It wasn't on purpose, I just lost track of some paperwork, and now my financial aid is a little bit at risk. But I'm going to fix it! I'm already looking into what I need to do to get it sorted out. 

And with the shop projects... I think maybe some of the people I work with have started depending on me a little less? Just because I've been a bit behind on my parts of the projects lately. I really hate letting people down, so I'm trying to be better about it. I promise I'm usually a hard worker! I just... things slipped a little. Is it bad that I let that happen? I'm really trying to get back on track.
Have your organizational difficulties been a persistent problem for you over the past few months?

Well, um... to be completely honest—and I really hope this doesn't make me sound completely irresponsible—but it's actually been a bit longer than just a few months. 

I guess... well, it's been a real problem for about two years and two months now? It basically started when I changed schools. I had to start managing the new business program and my accessories shop all at once, and there was just so much less structure than I was used to. 

I've really been trying my hardest to figure it out, I promise! It's just... taking me a little longer to adapt to the lack of structure than I thought it would. Is it okay that it's taken me this long to get a handle on it? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline, but I really am trying to do better!
Have your organizational difficulties been causing problems in your daily life or relationships most days over the past two years?

Um, well, I wouldn't say *most* days... I mean, I don't want you to think my life is a total disaster or anything! It's not like I'm constantly messing things up every single day. 

I guess... maybe it flares up sometimes? Like, if there's a big project due or a lot of orders for the shop all at once, things get a little chaotic. But most of the time, I try really hard to keep it together. My friends are super understanding, mostly, and I always apologize if I'm late or forget something. I try to make up for it, you know? 

So, no, I wouldn't say it's an everyday problem... just sort of a sometimes thing. Does that make sense? I just don't want to sound like I'm completely failing at everything. I'm really trying my best to keep everyone happy.
Have you felt like your difficulties with organization have significantly impacted your overall well-being or ability to function in daily life?

Um... well, I know I mentioned this earlier, and I really don't want it to sound worse than it is... but I guess it has impacted things a little bit. 

Like I said before, I did kind of miss those required steps for my program, and... well, my financial aid is at risk now because of it. I'm working on it, though! And, um, the people I collaborate with on shop projects... I think they have started depending on me less, like I was saying. I just hate the idea that I'm letting them down or that I can't handle my responsibilities. 

I really am trying to fix it all, I promise. Do you think that means it's significantly impacting my life? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right, but I don't want you to think I'm completely falling apart. I'm still functioning, mostly!
Do you feel like your organizational difficulties are causing you a lot of emotional pain or distress?

Oh, um... no, definitely not pain! I mean, I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining or, you know, being overly dramatic about things. It gets a little frustrating sometimes, sure, but... I wouldn't say it's causing me actual distress or anything like that. 

I'm actually a pretty upbeat person most of the time! I just try to look on the bright side and keep moving forward, you know? I mostly just get kind of annoyed with myself when I mess up or forget something for the shop, but I don't let it get me down for too long. 

Is it okay that I don't feel super distressed about it? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right idea, but I'm honestly doing okay emotionally! I really try to keep a positive attitude.
Do you ever avoid certain tasks or activities because they might make your organizational difficulties worse?

Um, avoid things? No, I don't think so. I mean, I really try to just tackle whatever comes my way, you know? I don't want to be the kind of person who just gives up or runs away from things that are a little hard. 

I guess... I mean, maybe sometimes if I know a project for the shop is going to take a ton of planning and sorting out all the little details, I might put it off for just a bit? But I always get to it eventually! I just like to make sure I'm in the right headspace for it so I don't mess it up for anyone else. 

But I wouldn't say I *avoid* anything completely. I'm always willing to try! Does that sound okay? I really do try to pull my weight and not let things intimidate me.
Have you ever had difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities?

Um, sustaining attention? I mean, I try really hard to pay attention, I promise I do! I don't want you to think I'm just ignoring people or not caring about my work. 

I guess... well, sometimes in class, or like, if I have to watch a really long video for my business assignments, I might drift off just a tiny bit? Like, I always start out listening really closely! But then, after a few minutes, my mind just sort of wanders to, um, like new charm designs I want to make for the shop, or ideas for orders. And then I realize I kind of missed what they were saying. 

But I always try to catch back up! It's not that I don't want to learn, I just get really excited about my projects. Is that normal? I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad student... I really do try to focus!
Do you often find yourself easily distracted by your surroundings or by other people when you're trying to focus on something?

Um, distracted by my surroundings? I don't... I don't think so! I mean, I really try to be respectful of where I am and what I'm supposed to be doing. 

If someone comes up and talks to me while I'm working, I'll definitely stop and chat with them, but mostly just because I want to be polite, you know? I'd hate to ever come across as rude or like I'm ignoring someone! But just random things happening around me in the room... no, I don't really notice that pulling me away. If I'm working on a new batch of charms or something, I just keep my hands busy and stay right there in the moment. 

Is it okay that I don't get distracted by that kind of stuff? I hope I'm answering these right for you! I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're supposed to be sitting still?

Um, restless? I mean, I really do try to sit quietly when I'm supposed to! I would hate to be a distraction to anyone else, you know? 

But, um... I guess maybe I do move around just a tiny bit? Like, if I have to sit through a long lecture or, um, those study group meetings, I don't always realize I'm doing it right away. But my leg might be bouncing, or I'll catch myself clicking a pen. Sometimes I'll just be messing with some extra beads or key rings I keep in my bag for the shop, just feeling them with my fingers. 

I don't mean to be fidgety, I promise! It just sort of happens before I even notice I'm doing it. But I always try to keep it hidden in my bag or under the desk so it doesn't bother anyone else. Is that okay? I hope that doesn't make me seem disrespectful or anything!
Do you often have difficulty completing tasks because you lose track of what you're doing or forget what you were supposed to do?

Um, losing track of what I'm doing? I really try my best to finish everything I start! I always want to make sure I'm doing a good job, especially if someone is counting on me. 

But... well, I guess sometimes, if there are a lot of steps, I might accidentally miss one? Like, if a teacher gives me a list of things to do for an assignment, or if I'm talking to someone at a vendor meeting for my shop and they give me a few instructions... I'll always jump right in and do the first part! I'm really good at getting started. But then, um, later on, I might realize I completely forgot to attach a form they asked for, or I didn't finish the last part of an order note. 

I don't do it on purpose, I swear! I always feel so awful when it happens, and I always apologize and try to fix it right away. I just get so focused on doing the first step right that the rest of it kind of... slips my mind? Does that make sense? I really hope people don't think I'm just being lazy or careless, because I really do care about getting it right!
Do you often interrupt others when they're talking or blurt out answers before they've finished asking a question?

Um, interrupting? Oh gosh, I really, really try not to do that. I know how rude it is, and I always want to make sure I'm being a good listener for people! 

But... um, I guess sometimes, like in group critiques or class discussions, I might accidentally jump in a little too soon? It's just that I get really engaged, and I think I know what they're asking, so I'll jump in with my answer before the other person is actually done talking. 

And then I realize I just guessed what they were going to say, and I feel *so* embarrassed. I always apologize right away! I'd hate for anyone to think I don't care about what they're sharing or that I'm trying to talk over them. The words just sort of slip out before my brain catches up to tell me to wait. 

Is that the kind of thing you mean? I really hope I don't sound like a bad person for doing that. I promise I'm trying to be better at waiting my turn to speak!
Do you often have trouble waiting for your turn or interrupting others when they're speaking, even when you're trying to be patient?

Um, waiting my turn? I really, really try to be patient, I promise! I know everyone else's time is just as important as mine, and I would never want to seem pushy or entitled. 

But... well, I guess waiting can be a little bit hard for me sometimes? Like, if I'm in a long line for financial aid, or if I'm waiting to ask a professor a question after class, or even during those group critiques I mentioned... I just get this sort of impatient feeling? And I don't mean to, but I'll find myself shifting my weight a lot, or stepping side to side. 

And, um, sometimes, if I've been waiting to speak for a while, I might accidentally cut in just a tiny bit before the other person is completely finished. I always feel terrible when it happens! I really don't mean to be rude, it just feels like the words have been backed up in my head for so long that they sort of spill out? 

I always apologize right away, though, and tell them to go ahead. I hope people know I'm not trying to rush them! Is it normal to struggle with waiting like that? I really am trying to be better about it.
